categories.main_business_segments: Nomura Real Estate Holdings operates six main business segments: Residential Development (condominiums, detached houses, senior housing, hotels), Urban Development (offices, commercial and logistics facilities), Overseas (real estate development and leasing abroad), Asset Management (REITs, private funds, securitized real estate products), Brokerage & CRE (real estate brokerage and consulting), and Property & Facility Management (operation and management of residential and commercial properties).
categories.core_technologies_production_methods: The company leverages advanced real estate development, project management, and property management expertise, with a focus on sustainable construction, energy efficiency (ZEH/ZEB standards), and digital transformation (DX) in operations. It also utilizes external and internal research for new technologies and business models, and applies rigorous risk management and quality assurance processes in design, construction, and asset management.
categories.primary_customers_markets: Key customers include individual homebuyers, corporate tenants, institutional investors, and property owners. The company serves residential buyers, commercial tenants (offices, retail, logistics), hotel guests, and investors in real estate funds, with a growing focus on high-net-worth individuals, inbound tourists, and overseas investors.
categories.geographic_coverage: Operations are primarily in Japan, especially the Tokyo metropolitan area, but the company has expanded into international markets including the UK, Singapore, Hong Kong, Vietnam, Thailand, China, and the Philippines. Domestic business remains dominant, but overseas projects are increasing in significance.
categories.supply_chain_position: Nomura Real Estate Holdings operates across the real estate value chain, from upstream (land acquisition and development) to midstream (construction, asset management) and downstream (sales, leasing, property management, brokerage). It also acts as a fund manager and investor in real estate assets.
categories.strategic_focus_rd_direction: Strategic priorities include maximizing customer and societal value, sustainability (decarbonization, biodiversity, circular design), digital transformation, and innovation in real estate services. R&D focuses on new technologies, business models, and sustainability initiatives, with a strong emphasis on human capital, diversity & inclusion, and wellness.
categories.revenue_model: Revenue is generated through property sales (residential and commercial), leasing income, property and facility management fees, brokerage commissions, asset management fees, and hotel operations. Additional income streams include equity investments and consulting services.
categories.key_competitors_industry_positioning: Major competitors include other large Japanese real estate developers such as Mitsui Fudosan, Mitsubishi Estate, and Sumitomo Realty & Development. Nomura Real Estate Holdings is positioned as a leading integrated developer with strengths in both residential and commercial sectors, and is recognized for its focus on sustainability and customer-centric innovation.
categories.financial_scale_growth_profile: For the fiscal year ending March 2025, consolidated revenue was ¥757.6 billion, with operating profit of ¥118.9 billion and net profit attributable to shareholders of ¥74.8 billion. The company has shown steady growth in revenue and profit over recent years, with a target of 8% average annual business profit growth and a focus on capital efficiency (ROE >10%). Total assets reached ¥2.69 trillion, and the group employs over 8,700 people.
categories.value_proposition_product_differentiatio: Nomura Real Estate Holdings differentiates itself through integrated real estate solutions, high-quality development and management, and a strong commitment to sustainability and social value. The company emphasizes customer happiness, wellness, and environmental responsibility, aiming to create long-term value for stakeholders through innovation, digitalization, and a people-centric approach.
